_comment: Execution role for the price ingestion Lambda. Data, not console clicks, for the same reasons the guardrail and alarms are (design.md 10.1). Apply with: python scripts/apply_iam.py --config config/iam-ingestion-role.json
_naming: The -dev suffix follows config/alarms.json: generated resources coexist with manually created ones during the migration to IaC (design.md 11, point 2).
description: Execution role for the Smart Grocery price ingestion Lambda.
_separation_note: Deliberately NOT the orchestrator's role. Ingestion writes prices and cannot invoke a model or touch the idempotency table; the orchestrator reads prices and cannot write them. Neither can do the other's job, so a defect in one cannot express itself through the other's permissions.

Statement._comment: Query is here so ingestion can diff before it writes. The first version of this role was write-only, and a write-only writer cannot know what it is about to change -- which is how unit_price_nzd "2490.00" reached six live rows with no signal. Reading the rows it is about to overwrite is the smallest permission that makes the write reportable. It is scoped to the base table only: the diff queries by store_key, which is the base table's partition key, so GSI1 is not needed and is not granted.

Append-only price history (src/history). WRITE ONLY, and the omission of Query is the point: ingestion appends a row per accepted product per capture date and never reads history back. The reader is ops and the data-quality reviewer, off the shopper path, under a different identity. No Delete and no UpdateItem either -- a history row is immutable by definition, so a role that could rewrite one could rewrite the baseline a deviation is measured against.
Statement._why_this_was_missing: src/history and the history write in ingestion/handler.py merged on 2026-09-02 (acc53fb) with neither this statement nor the table. The write is unconditional and runs AFTER the products write on an ENABLED daily schedule, so a scheduled refresh writes products and then fails on AccessDenied -- with no alarm, because the only ingestion alarm counts REJECTED ROWS and a branch that throws emits no datapoint. tests/test_ingestion.py fakes boto3.resource and routes by table name, so it proves the code writes history and structurally cannot see that the grant is absent. Same blind spot as docs/ARCHITECTURE.md 3f and 3g.

Statement._comment: Powertools Tracer. X-Ray segment writes are not resource-scopable -- the API takes no resource -- so * is the only expressible form.
